<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par53 />{{GHGmargin-letter|53|n}}
4. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} the ''shorter'' form with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} prevails for the jussive in the 3''rd masc.'' and {{GHGterm|fem.}} and 2''nd masc. sing.'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תַּגְדֵּל|translate=make not great}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַכְרֵת|translate=let Him cut off!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=4}}; even incorrectly {{GHGheb|text=תַּגֵּיד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=3}} and {{GHGheb|text=יַגֵּיד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=20}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=יַבְעֶר־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=4}}, where the jussive form is to be explained according to {{GHGpar|109|h}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יַֽאֲבֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=26}} before the principal pause. Similarly, after {{GHGheb|text=ו}} consec., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּבְדֵּל|translate=and He divided}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=4}}. On the other hand, ''î'' is almost always retained in the 1st sing., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וָאַֽשְׁמִיד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=9}} (but generally without {{GHGheb|text=י}}, as {{GHGheb|text=וָאַֽסְתִּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=39|verse=23}} f., &c.); cf. {{GHGpar|49|e}} and {{GHGpar|74|l}}, but also {{GHGpar|72|aa}}; in 1st plur. only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=3}}; in the 3rd sing. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=105|verse=28}}. With ''ă'' in the principal pause {{GHGheb|text=וַתּוֹתַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=14}}, and in the lesser pause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=4}}; before a sibilant (see {{GHGpar|29|q}}) {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּגַּשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=19}}; in the lesser pause {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּקַּף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=5}}. Before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} the Ṣere becomes {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽחֲזֶק־בּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=4}}. In the plural again, and before suffixes, ''î'' remains in the forms {{GHGheb|text=יַקְטִ֫ילוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּקְטִ֫ילוּ}}, even in the jussive and after {{GHGheb|text=ו}} consecutive, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּדְבִּ֫יקוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=22}}. The only exceptions, where the ''î'' is weakened to {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, are {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּדְרְכוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּדְבְּקוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=31|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=10|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעַבְרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=11|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאוֹצְרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=13}}, if it is {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=אצר}}, but probably {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲצַוֶּה}} is to be read, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=2|hidebook=1}}; perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=תַּהְכְּרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=3}} (according to others, {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}). The same weakening occurs also in the imperfect in 3rd and masc. sing. before suffixes, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=65|verse=10}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=20}}, unless the form be {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}={{GHGheb|text=וַיְעַקְשֵׁנִי}}, since the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} is not found elsewhere. It is hardly likely that in these isolated examples we have a trace of the ground-form, ''yaqtĭl'', or an Aramaism. More probably they are due partly to a misunderstanding of the defective writing, which is found, by a purely orthographic licence, in numerous other cases (even in 3rd sing. {{GHGheb|text=יַשְׁלִ֑ם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=28}}), and partly are intended, as ''formae mixtae'', to combine the forms of {{GHGterm|Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}. Instead of the firmly closed syllable, the Masora requires in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽדְשֵׁא}}, with euphonic Ga‛ya (see {{GHGpar|16|h}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|o}}
5. In the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGheb|text=מ֫וֹצֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=135|verse=7}} appears to be traceable to the ground-form, ''maqtĭl''; yet the Ṣere may also possibly be explained by the retraction of the tone. The Masora appears to require the weakening of the vowel to {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} (see above, n) in {{GHGheb|text=מַהְלְכִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=7}} (probably, however, {{GHGheb|text=מַֽהֲלָכִים}} should be read), also in {{GHGheb|text=מַחְלְמִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַעְזְרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=23}} (but as {{GHGheb|text=ם}} precedes, and accordingly dittography may well have taken place, the participle Qal is probably to be read in both places; the reading of the text is perhaps again intended to combine {{GHGterm|Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, see above, n), and in the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=מַחְצְרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=24}} &c. (where the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲצֹֽצְרִים}} is better).—The fem. is ordinarily pointed as {{GHGheb|text=מַזְכֶּ֫רֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=15}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַשֶּׂגֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=21}}; in pause {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=14}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|p}}
6. In the {{GHGterm|perfect}} there occur occasionally such forms as {{GHGheb|text=הֶכְלַ֫מְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=7}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=7}}; with the original ''ă'' in the first syllable {{GHGheb|text=וְהַרְאֵיתִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=5}}.—In {{GHGheb|text=אֶגְאָֽלְתִּי}}<ref>Most probably, however, {{GHGheb|text=גֵּאָ֫לְתִּי}} ({{GHGterm|perfect Piʿēl}}) is to be read, and the {{GHGheb|text=א}} is only an indication of the change of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} into the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, as also previously, by a change of punctuation, {{GHGheb|text=וְאדרכם}} and {{GHGheb|text=וְיֵז}} (instead of {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶדְ׳}} and {{GHGheb|text=וָיֵּז}}) are made future instead of past. Jewish exegesis applied these Edomoracles to the Roman (i.e. Christian) empire. So G. Moore in ''Theol. Literaturzeitung'', 1887, col. 292.</ref> ''I have stained'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=א}} stands at the beginning instead of {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, cf. above, k, on {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁכֵּים}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=וְהֶֽאֶזְנִ֫יחוּ}}<section end=par53 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
